description: The information bottleneck method compresses a random variable while preserving information about another. The LCS can be viewed as a compressed representation preserving maximal shared structure between two random strings. Rate-distortion theory gives fundamental limits, potentially yielding new bounds via the deletion channel capacity connection.
mathematical_formalization: Let X,Y be i.i.d. uniform binary strings of length n. The LCS S = LCS(X,Y) satisfies I(X;Y) >= I(X;S). Since X,Y are independent, I(X;Y)=0 but I(X;S|Y) provides constraints. Connection to deletion channel: gamma_2 is related to C_{del}(1/2) via the achievability of common subsequences.
implementation_hypothesis: Compute I(X; LCS(X,Y)) for small n by exact enumeration. Use the deletion channel relationship to derive upper bounds on gamma_2.
experiment_seed: For n=1..12, enumerate all binary string pairs. Compute LCS distribution. Calculate H(LCS), I(X;LCS). Relate to deletion channel capacity bounds.
